note_en: Chinese often expresses degree with 得 plus a result rather than a word like "very": 规则复杂得让人眼花 "the rules are so complicated they make your head spin." Everything after 得 measures how complicated, much like English "so... that...". The same 得 appears later in 备得太少 "stocking too little" and 备得太多 "stocking too much," where it introduces how an action is done.
